clue.text: Fine resort on the South Coast abolishing boundaries

indicators.note: removing the boundaries strips away the first and last letters of the resort's name

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A seaside town in southern England sweeps away its borders, to general approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abolishing boundaries' takes the outer B and N off BRIGHTON, a seaside town in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual British expressions of agreement, as when someone says 'okay' to a suggestion.

clue.text: Put under certain terms, partially

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is placed in custody on strict conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting a body under the ground.

clue.text: Flower for hero stupidly pinching gorgeous girl on the way up

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so the rearranged letters close around the other piece
acting stupidly suggests the letters of hero are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word girl's synonym is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl

explanation.surface: A foolish hero pinches a pretty girl's bottom while climbing, and offers a flower to make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorgeous girl' is a crossword favourite for a beauty; in a down clue 'on the way up' reads her upward, and 'pinching' puts that inside the jumbled hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The hellebore, or Christmas rose, is a winter-flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Gauge speed and energy

parts.note: OO gauge is a standard size of model railway track
mph, miles per hour, is a unit of speed

explanation.surface: A driver judges how fast the car is going and how much power it has.
explanation.walkthrough: OO gauge is the most common model railway scale in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour or energetic spirit.

clue.text: Retreat from a river in feint

indicators.note: in places the river's letter inside the pretence

parts.note: a feint is a pretence, a sham

explanation.surface: A boxer pulls back from the riverbank with a dummy punch.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat or hermitage.

clue.text: Original model of sports car found under bridge

indicators.note: in a down entry, the car coming beneath the bridge places it after the other piece

parts.note: an arch is a bridge-like curved structure, and a bridge may be an arch
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: An early prototype of a sports car turns up parked beneath a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the first example from which later copies are modelled.

clue.text: Ran quickly, loathing to lose time

indicators.note: losing means dropping a letter from the word for loathing

parts.note: loathing is hatred

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted off, hating to waste a single moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run fast, like a hare, so the past tense means sprinted.

clue.text: Consequences of following science in America

parts.note: after means following
Americans say math where Britons say maths

explanation.surface: A study of what follows from scientific work done in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the set of results that follow a significant event.

clue.text: Entertained a thought

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: Someone toyed with an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained by something means finding it funny or diverting.

clue.text: Period before Christmas opening, after a dubious beginning

indicators.note: after places the opening following the other pieces
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A shop opens its Christmas season after a shaky start.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the four-week church season leading up to Christmas.

clue.text: Turning back, unable to move around accommodation

indicators.note: Turning back says the hidden letters are read backwards
around says the answer's letters lie within the surrounding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stranded traveller, unable to go on, turns round to find a room for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'around accommodation' as the definition, but 'around' is the hiding indicator: LETOM sits inside 'unable to move', and 'Turning back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is roadside lodging for motorists, a type of accommodation.

clue.text: Staff deserved getting soaked

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
rated can mean merited or deserved, as in 'rated a mention'

explanation.surface: Employees who earned it are getting drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Macerated food has been softened by steeping in liquid.

clue.text: Cry coming from church by loose rocks on side of mountain

parts.words: loose rocks on side of mountain
parts.note: scree is loose stones on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: A shout rings out from a chapel beside a rocky mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a shrill, piercing shout or call.

clue.text: Doreen's dicky back

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, signalling the letters are disordered

parts.note: the name with its apostrophe-s supplies seven letters

explanation.surface: A woman named Doreen has a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky' is British slang for unsound, as in 'a dicky heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: To back something is to support or approve it.

clue.text: Finding one's bay, needing a drink outside

indicators.note: outside says the thirsty word wraps around the others

parts.note: dry means thirsty
one is I, so one's is I'S
a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: Someone finds their bay and fancies a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, the result of finding.

clue.text: Sort of water cycle to play down

parts.note: soft water is water low in minerals
to pedal is to cycle

explanation.surface: A child asks about the water cycle and an adult plays it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to make something seem less important than it is.

clue.text: A necessity for working last seen around the west of Ireland

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the letter from Ireland
working suggests the letters of 'last seen' being put to work in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the westernmost or leftmost letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A vital tool for work was last seen in the west of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles LASTSEEN to ESSENTAL; 'around' puts I, the west of Ireland, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential is something indispensable, a must-have item.

clue.text: Bribery is hard work!

definitions.meaning: corruption, using a position for illicit gain

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that corruption takes effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has two senses: political corruption, and toil.

clue.text: Had dinner in good hotel on river providing accommodation

indicators.note: in places the meal word inside the other letters

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
ate means had a meal
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Someone dined at a fine riverside hotel offering rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, among others.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is a lodging at an estate's gate, a form of housing.

clue.text: Faux pas from the boss, finishing early

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss

explanation.surface: The boss made a blunder by leaving work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaffer' is British slang for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing social blunder.

clue.text: Gather, having married for name, son shines

indicators.note: married is M and name is N, so the word has M in place of N

parts.note: to glean is to gather

explanation.surface: Someone learns that a woman took her husband's name, and her son is a shining success.
explanation.walkthrough: M for married and N for name are standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To gleam is to shine brightly, and the clue uses the third person.

clue.text: Whose past is fashioned in a harsh working environment?

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are made into another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whose history was formed in harsh working conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory with very poor working conditions.

clue.text: Sky pilots may be spared at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ship's chaplains may be excused duties on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky pilots' is slang for clergymen, especially military chaplains.
explanation.definitionFit: Padres are chaplains, jokingly called sky pilots for guiding souls heavenward.

clue.text: Account for one in former scheme

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone must justify an individual's part in a past plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain is to give the reasons for something.

clue.text: Improvisation from a politician travelling across Germany

indicators.note: crossing means the politician spans over the country's letter

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A politician touring Germany makes it up as he goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad lib is a remark made up on the spot.

clue.text: A cast around in the morning, feeling embarrassed

indicators.note: around says the cast word goes outside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake sheds skin
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: An acting troupe goes about red-faced at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed describes a feeling of guilt or embarrassment.

clue.text: Helps president with heartless tasks

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Assistants aid the president with jobs lacking passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Abets means assists, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Intended to make new investment in animal product

indicators.note: investment, putting something in, means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: meat is an animal product

explanation.surface: A fresh investment opportunity in livestock farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant means planned or intended.

clue.text: Earned the right of choice in business making cake

parts.note: made means earned, as in made money

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the business word

parts.note: a line is a line of business

indicators.note: the rightmost letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: Someone earns the right to choose a business making cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small French sponge cake.

clue.text: In focus, a general practice

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A general's typical procedure kept in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means customary practice.

clue.text: World travel around the end of April — before graduate left

indicators.note: around means the travel word wraps around the letter

parts.note: go means travel

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A gap-year graduate travels the world in late April before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Global and world both describe something worldwide, as in world trade.

clue.text: The girl's keeping endless pets in bed linen

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the pronoun word holds the middle letters

parts.note: the girl's means she's, she is

indicators.note: endless removes the ends, leaving the middle letters

explanation.surface: A girl keeps pets in her bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets are bed coverings, the main item of bed linen.
